structure:
A single 37-line Markdown ruling file (workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-10-26.md) from Sam, dated 26 October 2026, on Save and return to overview. It runs: a heading (line 1); the framing of the BA's find that Save and return to overview skips the checks Save and continue makes on upload documents, origin and main reason for import (lines 3-4); the BA's expected behaviour as a quoted Given/When/Then of three lines (lines 6-8); Sam's 23 October quote, one line, telling the session not to assume the earlier ruling is right because the BA raised it (lines 10-12); Sam's 26 October quote on a documents-only fix, two lines, refusing documents behaving differently and calling for consistency (lines 14-17); then the main session's reading as 4 numbered claims (lines 19-37). Claims 1 and 2 cover Save and return to overview's checks and that no page, upload documents included, is an exception; claim 1 is marked as replacing c-211 and c-313, claim 2 as built as inc-232 in themes/design-snagging-followups. Lines 29-31 then carry a third Sam quote, one line ('happy with recommendations on both'), on the two held engineering-review questions, which claims 3 (Enter in an Identification details card for several animals saves that card, built as inc-224) and 4 (Notification submitted lists the ITAHC as still to upload whenever none was uploaded, built as inc-230) read. Every claim is marked New. Scope is the whole file, so nothing is left out. It is one part: the whole file, well inside what one agent reads word for word.

Extracted in 1 part:
Part 1, Whole ruling: Part 1 of 1, the whole file: workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-10-26.md, 37 lines of Markdown, read in full. It is laid out as: a heading (line 1); the main session's framing of the BA's find that Save and return to overview skips the checks Save and continue makes on upload documents, origin and main reason for import (lines 3-4); the BA's expected behaviour as a quoted three-line Given/When/Then with the page name left as "xxxx" (lines 6-8); Sam's 23 October one-line quote withdrawing the assumption that his earlier ruling is right because the BA raised the issue (lines 10-12); Sam's 26 October two-line quote refusing a documents-only fix, saying documents must not behave differently, that the BA has given the behaviour we should have and that it should be consistent (lines 14-17); numbered claims 1 and 2, the main session's reading of those quotes, on Save and return making exactly the same checks on every page with both buttons in live animals and high-risk plants (replacing c-211 and c-313) and on no page being an exception, upload documents included (built as inc-232 in themes/design-snagging-followups) (lines 19-26); Sam's 26 October one-line quote 'happy with recommendations on both' on the two held engineering-review questions, after a recommendation for each (lines 28-30); and numbered claims 3 and 4, reading that quote as Enter in an Identification details card for several animals saving that card (built as inc-224) and Notification submitted listing the ITAHC as still to upload whenever none was uploaded (built as inc-230) (lines 32-37). Every numbered claim is marked New. Covered: the BA framing and quoted behaviour, all three of Sam's quotes, all four numbered claims checked clause by clause against the quotes, the conflict and increment references the claims cite, and the points the ruling leaves open (the unquoted recommendations, the sets other than live animals and high-risk plants, the unnamed earlier ruling, the unnamed page in the BA scenario).

claims.statement: Save and return to overview skips the checks that Save and continue makes, on the upload documents, origin and main reason for import pages.
claims.quote: On the BA's find that Save and return to overview skips the checks Save and continue makes (upload documents, origin, main reason for import), and the BA's expected behaviour:
claims.note: The current, unwanted behaviour as the ruling frames it, found by the BA. The three pages named are where it was found, not necessarily the only pages affected.

claims.statement: On selecting either "Save and continue" or "Save and return to overview", the trader sees an error message for each answer that is missing or not valid.
claims.quote:
When I select "Save and continue" or "Save and return to overview"
Then I should see an error message for each answer that is missing or not valid
claims.note: The BA's expected behaviour, quoted in the ruling and endorsed by Sam at lines 16-17 ("He's given you the behaviour that we should have").

claims.statement: After selecting either save button with an answer missing or not valid, the trader remains on the page.
claims.quote: And I should remain on the "xxxx" page
claims.note: The page name is left as the placeholder "xxxx" in the quote, so the scenario is written for any page rather than a named one.

claims.statement: Sam's earlier ruling on this behaviour is not to be assumed right, because the BA is the one raising the issue.
claims.quote: dont assume my ruling from the other day is right, this is teh BA raising the issue
claims.note: Quoted with the source's own spelling. It withdraws the earlier ruling's standing; Sam's 26 October quote then supplies the behaviour.

claims.statement: Upload documents must not behave differently from other pages: a documents-only fix is refused.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-26.md lines 14-17 (Sam, 26 October, on a documents-only fix, quoted)
claims.quote: No, we don't want fucking documents behaving differently. He's given you the behaviour that we should have. It should be consistent.
claims.note: Quoted verbatim including the expletive, as the extract rules require; the "No" answers a proposal to fix documents alone.

claims.statement: The BA's expected behaviour is the behaviour the service should have.
claims.quote: He's given you the behaviour that we should have.
claims.note: Adopts claims 002 and 003 (the BA's Given/When/Then) as the owner's decision.

claims.statement: The behaviour of the save buttons should be consistent.
claims.quote: It should be consistent.

claims.statement: Save and return to overview makes exactly the same checks as Save and continue.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-26.md lines 19-20 (claim 1), resting on lines 6-7 and 16-17
claims.quote: Save and return to overview makes exactly the same checks as Save and continue, on every page that has both buttons, in live animals and high-risk plants.
claims.note: Marked New in the ruling. The quoted BA behaviour ("When I select \"Save and continue\" or \"Save and return to overview\"") and Sam's endorsement say this in so many words.

claims.statement: The same-checks rule applies on every page that has both buttons, in the live animals frontend and in the high-risk plants frontend; this follows because Sam's quotes say only that the behaviour should be consistent and that documents must not differ, and the services are named in the main session's reading rather than in any quote.
claims.quote: on every page that has both buttons, in live animals and high-risk plants
claims.note: Marked New in the ruling. The scope (every page with both buttons; live animals and high-risk plants) is the main session's reading, not words Sam's quotes use.

claims.statement: On any missing or invalid answer the trader stays on the page with an error for each one, and what the trader entered is kept; the staying and the per-answer errors are the BA's quoted behaviour, while keeping the entry is the main session's reading, which no quote states.
claims.quote: On any missing or invalid answer the trader stays on the page with an error for each one and what they entered is kept
claims.note: Marked New in the ruling. Claims 002 and 003 carry the verbatim half (error per answer, remain on the page); only "what they entered is kept" is beyond the quotes.

claims.statement: With no missing or invalid answers, Save and return to overview saves the answers and shows the overview; the ruling's numbered claim states this but none of Sam's quotes mention the success path.
claims.quote: with none, the answers are saved and the overview is shown
claims.note: Marked New in the ruling.

claims.statement: This decision replaces conflict c-211 (the soft save) and c-313 (its plants counterpart), which let Save and return skip blank required answers; Sam's quotes withdraw the earlier ruling and refuse a partial fix but never cite the conflict ids, so the mapping is the main session's reading.
claims.quote: Replaces c-211 (the soft save) and c-313 (its plants counterpart), which let Save and return skip blank required answers.
claims.note: Marked New in the ruling. Conflict references recorded: c-211 (live animals soft save) and c-313 (high-risk plants counterpart). Rests on Sam's 23 October quote (claim 004) and his 26 October quote (claims 005-007).

claims.statement: No page is an exception to the same-checks rule, and upload documents follows the same rule as every other page.
claims.quote: No page is an exception. Upload documents follows the same rule:
claims.note: Marked New in the ruling. Sam's quote says it in so many words: "we don't want fucking documents behaving differently" and "It should be consistent." Built as inc-232 in themes/design-snagging-followups.
